---
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
A code $C \in \Sigma^n$ is $(\rho, L)$-list decodable if for every $z \in \Sigma^n$, the number of codewords in $c \in C$ satisfying $\operatorname{Hamm}(c, z) \le \rho n$ is at most $L$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
A code $C \in \Sigma^n$ is $(\rho, \ell, L)$-list recoverable if for every input lists $S_i \subset \Sigma$, $|S_i| \le \ell, \forall i \in [n]$, the number of codewords in $c \in C$ satisfying 
    \[
        |\{ i \in [n] | c_i \not\in S_i\}| \le \rho n
    \]
    is at most $L$.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{def:qld-intro}
A stabilizer code \(Q\) of block length \(n\) is
\((\rho,L)\)-\emph{quantum list decodable} (QLD) if, for every
possible syndrome \(\sigma\), there are at most \(L\) pairwise
stabilizer-distinct Pauli errors of weight at most \(\rho n\)
consistent with \(\sigma\).
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\label{def:qlr-intro}
A stabilizer code \(Q\) of block length \(n\) is
\((\rho,\ell,L)\)-\emph{quantum list recoverable} (QLR) if, for every
syndrome \(\sigma\) and every collection of local Pauli lists
\(\mathcal E_1,\ldots,\mathcal E_n\) with
\(|\mathcal E_i|\le\ell\), there are at most \(L\) pairwise
stabilizer-distinct Pauli errors \(F\) with syndrome \(\sigma\)
satisfying \(\operatorname{dis}(F,\mathcal E)\le\rho n\).
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
For a CSS code $Q=(C_1,C_2)$, $Q$ is $(\rho, \ell, L)$-quantum list recoverable if for every collection of local Pauli lists
\(\mathcal E_1,\ldots,\mathcal E_n\) with
\(|\mathcal E_i|\le\ell\), if $c_1,\ldots,c_j \in N_Q$ have the same syndrome, satisfy \(\operatorname{dis}(c_i,\mathcal E)\le\rho n\) $\forall i \in [j]$, and $c_i + S_Q$ are all pairwise distinct cosets, then $j \le L$.

A CSS code $Q=(C_1,C_2)$ is $(\rho, L)$-quantum list decodable if it is $(\rho, 1, L)$-list recoverable.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:informal-qlcl}
For fixed witness width and a fixed flagged local profile, a random nested pair $S\subseteq C\subseteq\mathbb F_q^n$ has the following threshold behavior.  If the quotient-minor gap is negative by $\epsilon$, then the flagged witness is absent with probability at least $1-q^{-\epsilon+O(1)}$.  If the quotient-minor gap is positive by $\epsilon$, then the flagged witness is present with probability at least $1-q^{-\epsilon+O(1)}$.  After a union bound over profiles and flags, the same criterion gives threshold theorems for LCL properties in both the parity-check and uniform nested-subspace ensembles.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
\label{rsd:def:relative}
Let \(S\subseteq N\subseteq W^n\), let \(r\in\mathbb N\), and let \(\alpha\in[0,1]\).  The pair \((N,S)\) is an \emph{\(\alpha\)-relative subspace design up to dimension \(r\)} if for every subspace \(A\le N\) satisfying
\[
  1\le \dim A\le r,
  \qquad A\cap S=\{0\},
\]
one has
\begin{equation}\label{rsd:eq:relative-design}
   \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \dim(A\cap K_i)
      \le \alpha\dim A .
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\[
   \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \dim\pi_i(A)
      \ge (1-\alpha)\dim A .
\]
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
\label{rsd:def:css-sd}
Let \(Q=Q(C_1,C_2)\) be the CSS code defined by \(C_2\subseteq C_1\subseteq W^n\).  We say that \(Q\) is an \emph{\((\alpha_X,\alpha_Z)\)-CSS subspace design up to dimension \(r\)} if
\[
   (C_1,C_2)\quad\text{is an }\alpha_X\text{-relative subspace design up to dimension }r,
\]
and
\[
   (C_2^\perp,C_1^\perp)\quad\text{is an }\alpha_Z\text{-relative subspace design up to dimension }r.
\]
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:informal-inner}
For every fixed witness dimension $r$, field $\mathbb F_q$, bounded-entropy folded profile class, and target inner CSS rate, there are constant-size folded CSS pairs whose $X$- and $Z$-normalizer sectors are AEL-robust folded qLCL gadgets at the rate-plus-slack thresholds supplied by the random qLCL calculation.  Since the size is constant, the gadgets can be found by exhaustive search.  Specializing to kernel profiles gives AEL-robust relative subspace-design gadgets.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:main-informal}
Fix a target quantum rate $R\in(0,1)$, a witness dimension $r$, an accuracy $\varepsilon>0$, and any pair of bounded-entropy folded profile classes for the two sectors.  There is an explicit folded CSS code family with folded block length $n$, constant fold size depending only on $(R,r,\varepsilon)$ and the class entropy exponent, and quantum rate at least $R-O(\varepsilon)$, containing no injective-logical LCL witness for the given classes up to dimension $r$ at thresholds
\[
   \alpha_X,\alpha_Z\le \frac{1+R}{2}+O(\varepsilon).
\]
Specializing the classes to kernel profiles, the family is an $(\alpha_X,\alpha_Z)$-CSS subspace design up to dimension $r$.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:inf-list-dec}
    There exists an infinite family of qLDPC codes with rate $R_Q$ that are $(\rho, L)$-quantum list decodable, with $\rho$ satisfying:
    \[
        \rho < \frac{L}{L+1}\cdot \frac{(1-R_Q-\varepsilon)}{2}.
    \]
    The alphabet size is a constant, and depends only on $R, \varepsilon, L$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:inf-list-rec}
    There exists an infinite family of qLDPC codes that are $(\rho, \ell, L)$-quantum list recoverable such that
    \[
        \rho \le (1-R_Q-\varepsilon)/2 \quad L \le (\ell/\varepsilon)^{O(R/\varepsilon)}.
    \]
    The alphabet size is a constant that only depends on $R, \varepsilon, \ell, L$.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
Fix $b\in\mathbb N$.  A \emph{$b$-local profile} of length $n$ is a sequence
\[
       \mathcal V=(V_1,\ldots,V_n),\qquad V_i\leq \mathbb F_q^b .
\]
For $U\leq \mathbb F_q^b$, define its profile mass
\begin{equation}\label{qlcl:eq:profile-mass}
       a_\mathcal V(U) \coloneqq \sum_{i=1}^n \dim(V_i\cap U).
\end{equation}
Let
\[
       \mathcal M_\mathcal V(U) \coloneqq \{A\in\mathbb F_q^{n\times b}: A_{i,*}\in V_i\cap U\text{ for every }i\}.
\]
Thus $|\mathcal M_\mathcal V(U)|=q^{a_\mathcal V(U)}$.  Let
\[
       \mathcal M_\mathcal V^{=}(U) \coloneqq \{A\in\mathcal M_\mathcal V(U):\operatorname{row}(A)=U\}.
\]
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:lem:exact-row-count}
Let $\mathcal V$ be a $b$-local profile and let $U\leq \mathbb F_q^b$.  Then
\[
       |\mathcal M_\mathcal V^{=}(U)|\leq q^{a_\mathcal V(U)}.
\]
Moreover, if
\[
       a_\mathcal V(U)-a_\mathcal V(W)\geq \epsilon
       \qquad\text{for every proper }W<U,
\]
then
\[
       |\mathcal M_\mathcal V^{=}(U)|
       \geq q^{a_\mathcal V(U)}\left(1-q^{-\epsilon+b^2}\right).
\]
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The upper bound is immediate.  A matrix in $\mathcal M_\mathcal V(U)$ whose row span is not $U$ lies in $\mathcal M_\mathcal V(W)$ for some proper subspace $W<U$.  The number of subspaces of $\mathbb F_q^b$ is at most $q^{b^2}$.  Hence
\[
   |\mathcal M_\mathcal V(U)\setminus \mathcal M_\mathcal V^{=}(U)|
   \leq \sum_{W<U}q^{a_\mathcal V(W)}
   \leq q^{b^2}q^{a_\mathcal V(U)-\epsilon}.
\]
Subtracting from $|\mathcal M_\mathcal V(U)|=q^{a_\mathcal V(U)}$ proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
A \emph{nested pair} is an inclusion of linear codes
\[
       S\subseteq C\subseteq \mathbb F_q^n .
\]
The quotient $C/S$ is called the logical quotient.
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:def:logical-row-space}
For a nested pair $S\subseteq C$ and a matrix $A\in\mathbb F_q^{n\times b}$ whose columns lie in $C$, define
\[
       K_S(A) \coloneqq \lambda_A^{-1}(S) = \{x\in\mathbb F_q^b:Ax\in S\}.
\]
The \emph{logical row space} of $A$ modulo $S$ is
\[
       \Lambda_S(A)=K_S(A)^\perp\leq \mathbb F_q^b .
\]
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
Let
\[
       \operatorname{LDist}_b
       =\{T\leq\mathbb F_q^b:\forall j\neq k\text{ there exists }t\in T\text{ with }t_j\neq t_k\}.
\]
Equivalently, $T\in\operatorname{LDist}_b$ iff $e_j-e_k\notin T^\perp$ for all $j\neq k$.
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:lem:logical-distinctness}
Let $A\in\mathbb F_q^{n\times b}$ have columns in $C$.  The $b$ columns of $A$ are pairwise distinct as elements of $C/S$ iff
\[
       \Lambda_S(A)\in\operatorname{LDist}_b .
\]
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Columns $j$ and $k$ represent the same coset modulo $S$ iff $A(e_j-e_k)\in S$, i.e. iff $e_j-e_k\in K_S(A)=\Lambda_S(A)^\perp$.  This is exactly the negation of the defining condition for $\operatorname{LDist}_b$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
For fixed locality $b$, define
\[
       \operatorname{Flag}_b=\{(U,T):T\leq U\leq\mathbb F_q^b\}.
\]
For dimensions $m_0\leq m_1$, a flag $(U,T)$ is called \emph{$(m_0,m_1)$-feasible} if
\[
       \dim(U/T)\leq m_0,
       \qquad
       \dim T\leq m_1-m_0 .
\]
It is called \emph{parity-feasible} for $(m_0,m_1)$ if the second inequality holds; the first is not required.
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:def:flagged-realization}
Let $S\subseteq C$ be a nested pair, let $\mathcal V$ be a $b$-local profile, and let $(U,T)\in\operatorname{Flag}_b$.  We say that $S\subseteq C$ \emph{realizes} $(\mathcal V,U,T)$ if there exists a matrix $A\in\mathbb F_q^{n\times b}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item $A_{i,*}\in V_i$ for every $i\in[n]$;
    \item $\operatorname{row}(A)=U$;
    \item every column of $A$ lies in $C$;
    \item $\Lambda_S(A)=T$.
\end{enumerate}
Such an $A$ is called a realization of $(\mathcal V,U,T)$.
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:lem:auto-feasibility}
Let $S\subseteq C\subseteq\mathbb F_q^n$ have $\dim S=m_0$ and $\dim C=m_1$.  If $S\subseteq C$ realizes $(\mathcal V,U,T)$, then $(U,T)$ is $(m_0,m_1)$-feasible.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Let $A$ be a realization and write $B=\operatorname{im}\lambda_A\leq C$.  Then $\dim B=\dim U$.  The image of $K_S(A)$ under $\lambda_A$ is exactly $B\cap S$, and its kernel is $\ker\lambda_A=U^\perp$.  Since $K_S(A)=T^\perp$,
\[
       \dim(B\cap S)
       =\dim T^\perp-\dim U^\perp
       =\dim U-\dim T.
\]
Thus $\dim(U/T)\leq\dim S=m_0$.  The induced image of $B$ in $C/S$ has dimension $\dim T$, so $\dim T\leq\dim(C/S)=m_1-m_0$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- definition-14: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:def:qlcl-property}
A \emph{$b$-quotient LCL property} of nested pairs of length $n$ is specified by a finite family $\mathcal F$ of $b$-local profiles and a set $\mathcal D\subseteq\mathcal L(\mathbb F_q^b)$ of allowed logical row spaces.  A nested pair $S\subseteq C$ satisfies $\mathcal P(\mathcal F,\mathcal D)$ if there exist
\[
       \mathcal V\in\mathcal F,
       \qquad
       (U,T)\in\operatorname{Flag}_b,
       \qquad
       U\neq 0,
       \qquad
       T\in\mathcal D,
\]
such that $S\subseteq C$ realizes $(\mathcal V,U,T)$.  Thus the all-zero matrix is not a witness.
<!-- end definition-14 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:lem:quotient-witness}
Let $S\subseteq C$ realize $(\mathcal V,U,T)$ via $A \in \mathbb F_q^{n \times b}$.  Let $W<U$ be a proper subspace, and let
\[
       \rho:U\to \overline U
\]
be a surjective linear map with kernel $W$.  Choose a matrix $B\in\mathbb F_q^{b\times d}$, where $d=\dim\overline U$, such that right multiplication by $B$ restricts to $\rho$ on $U$.  Put $D=AB$ and define the quotient profile $\overline \mathcal V = (\overline V_1,\ldots, \overline V_n)$:
\[
       \overline V_i=\rho(V_i\cap U)\leq \overline U\leq\mathbb F_q^d.
\]
Then $D$ is a realization, for the same nested pair, of the quotient flag
\[
       (\overline\mathcal V,\overline U,\rho(T)).
\]
Moreover
\[
       \dim\rho(T)=\dim T-\dim(T\cap W).
\]
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
The rows of $D$ are obtained by applying $\rho$ to the rows of $A$, hence $D_{i,*}\in\overline V_i$ and $\operatorname{row}(D)=\rho(\operatorname{row}(A))=\overline U$.  The columns of $D$ are linear combinations of the columns of $A$, so they lie in $C$.

It remains to identify the logical row space.  Let $K=K_S(A)=T^\perp$.  For $y\in\mathbb F_q^d$,
\[
       Dy\in S
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
       A(By)\in S
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
       By\in K.
\]
Thus $K_S(D)=B^{-1}K$.  Taking orthogonal complements gives
\[
       \Lambda_S(D)=(B^{-1}K)^\perp=T B=\rho(T),
\]
where the last equality uses that right multiplication by $B$ is $\rho$ on $U$ and $T\leq U$.  The kernel of $\rho|_T$ is $T\cap W$, proving the dimension formula.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- definition-15: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:def:pcss}
The ensemble $\operatorname{\mathsf{PCSS}}(n,q;m_0,m_1)$ is sampled by choosing independent uniformly random matrices
\[
       H_C\in\mathbb F_q^{a\times n},
       \qquad
       H_S\in\mathbb F_q^{c\times n},
\]
and setting
\[
       C=\ker H_C,
       \qquad
       S=\ker H_C\cap\ker H_S.
\]
Then $S\subseteq C$.
<!-- end definition-15 -->
<!-- definition-16: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:def:potential}
For a flag $(U,T)$, write $u=\dim U$ and $t=\dim T$.  Define its random-nested-pair cost by
\begin{equation}\label{qlcl:eq:flag-cost}
       \kappa_{m_0,m_1}(U,T)
       \coloneqq a u+c(u-t)
       =(n-m_0)(u-t)+(n-m_1)t .
\end{equation}
For a profile $\mathcal V$, define the qLCL potential
\begin{equation}\label{qlcl:eq:potential}
       \Phi_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)
       \coloneqq a_\mathcal V(U)-\kappa_{m_0,m_1}(U,T).
\end{equation}
<!-- end definition-16 -->
<!-- definition-17: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:def:gamma}
For $U\neq 0$ and $T\leq U$, define
\begin{equation}\label{qlcl:eq:gamma}
       \Gamma_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)
        \coloneqq \min_{W<U}
       \left(
          \Phi_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)
          -\Phi_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,W,T\cap W)
       \right).
\end{equation}
The minimum is over proper subspaces $W$ of $U$.
<!-- end definition-17 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:lem:gamma-mass}
If $\Gamma_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)\geq \epsilon$, then for every proper $W<U$,
\[
       a_\mathcal V(U)-a_\mathcal V(W)\geq \epsilon .
\]
Consequently
\[
       |\mathcal M_\mathcal V^{=}(U)|
       \geq q^{a_\mathcal V(U)}(1-q^{-\epsilon+b^2}).
\]
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Let $T_W=T\cap W$.  The cost difference
\[
       \kappa(U,T)-\kappa(W,T_W)
       =(n-m_0)\bigl((u-t)-(\dim W-\dim T_W)\bigr)
        +(n-m_1)(t-\dim T_W)
\]
is nonnegative because $T_W=T\cap W$.  Therefore
\[
       a_\mathcal V(U)-a_\mathcal V(W)
       =\bigl(\Phi(U,T)-\Phi(W,T_W)\bigr)
        +\bigl(\kappa(U,T)-\kappa(W,T_W)\bigr)
       \geq \epsilon .
\]
Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:exact-row-count} gives the count.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:lem:fixed-matrix-prob}
Let $A\in\mathbb F_q^{n\times b}$ have row space $U$ of dimension $u$, and let $T\leq U$ have dimension $t$.  In the ensemble $\operatorname{\mathsf{PCSS}}(n,q;m_0,m_1)$,
\[
 \operatorname{Pr}[ A_{*,1},\ldots,A_{*,b}\in C\text{ and }\Lambda_S(A)=T]
   = q^{-\kappa_{m_0,m_1}(U,T)}\,\iota(c,t),
\]
where
\[
       \iota(c,t)=
       \begin{cases}
       \displaystyle\prod_{j=0}^{t-1}(1-q^{j-c}), & t\leq c,\\[1ex]
       0, & t>c,
       \end{cases}
\]
with the convention $\iota(c,0)=1$.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
The event that all columns of $A$ lie in $C$ is $H_C A=0$.  Since $\operatorname{rank}(A)=u$, this gives $a u$ independent linear equations on $H_C$, and has probability $q^{-au}$.

Condition on $H_C A=0$.  The matrix $H_SA$ is a uniformly random linear map
\[
       \mathbb F_q^b/\ker\lambda_A\cong \mathbb F_q^b/U^\perp\longrightarrow \mathbb F_q^c .
\]
The condition $\Lambda_S(A)=T$ is equivalent to
\[
       \ker(H_SA)=T^\perp.
\]
Modulo $U^\perp$, this says that a random map from the $u$-dimensional domain vanishes exactly on the fixed $(u-t)$-dimensional subspace $T^\perp/U^\perp$.  Vanishing on that subspace has probability $q^{-c(u-t)}$.  After quotienting by it, the induced map from a $t$-dimensional space to $\mathbb F_q^c$ must be injective, which has probability $\prod_{j=0}^{t-1}(1-q^{j-c})$ if $t\leq c$ and probability $0$ otherwise.  Multiplying by $q^{-au}$ gives the formula.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:cor:one-flag-expectation}
Let
\[
       X_{\mathcal V,U,T}=\#\{A\in\mathcal M_\mathcal V^{=}(U): A_{*,j}\in C\text{ for all }j,\ \Lambda_S(A)=T\}.
\]
Then
\[
       \operatorname{\mathbb{E}} [X_{\mathcal V,U,T}]
       \leq q^{\Phi_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)}.
\]
If $\Gamma_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)\geq\epsilon$ and $t\leq c$, then
\[
       \operatorname{\mathbb{E}} [X_{\mathcal V,U,T}]
       \geq q^{\Phi_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)}
          (1-q^{-\epsilon+b^2})\,\iota(c,t).
\]
In particular, if $\epsilon\geq 2b^2+1$ and $t\leq c$, then
\[
       \operatorname{\mathbb{E}} [X_{\mathcal V,U,T}]\geq q^{\Phi_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)-2b^2}.
\]
All expectations are over the random ensemble $\operatorname{\mathsf{PCSS}}(n,q;m_0,m_1)$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
The upper bound follows from $|\mathcal M_\mathcal V^{=}(U)|\le q^{a_\mathcal V(U)}$ and Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:fixed-matrix-prob}.  The lower bound follows from Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:gamma-mass} and Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:fixed-matrix-prob}.  For the final displayed bound, note that $\iota(c,t)\geq q^{-t}\geq q^{-b}$ when $t\leq c$, and $1-q^{-\epsilon+b^2}\geq q^{-1}$ under the stated numerical assumption.  Weakening constants gives the stated $2b^2$ loss.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:lem:minor-potential}
Let $W<U$, set $T_W=T\cap W$, and let $\rho:U\to\overline U$ be a quotient map with kernel $W$.  Let $\overline\mathcal V$ be the quotient profile $\overline V_i=\rho(V_i\cap U)$ and let $\overline T=\rho(T)$.  Then
\[
       \Phi_{m_0,m_1}(\overline\mathcal V,\overline U,\overline T)
       =\Phi_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)-\Phi_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,W,T_W).
\]
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
For every coordinate $i$,
\[
       \dim\overline V_i
       =\dim(V_i\cap U)-\dim(V_i\cap W).
\]
Therefore $a_{\overline\mathcal V}(\overline U)=a_\mathcal V(U)-a_\mathcal V(W)$.  Also
\[
       \dim\overline U=\dim U-\dim W,
       \qquad
       \dim\overline T=\dim T-\dim(T\cap W),
\]
so the flag cost subtracts in the same way.  Combining these identities proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:prop:fixed-subcritical}
If $U\neq0$, $T\leq U$, and
\[
       \Gamma_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)\leq -\epsilon,
\]
then, for $(S,C)\sim\operatorname{\mathsf{PCSS}}(n,q;m_0,m_1)$,
\[
       \operatorname{Pr}[(S,C)\text{ realizes }(\mathcal V,U,T)]\leq q^{-\epsilon}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Choose $W<U$ such that
\[
       \Phi(\mathcal V,U,T)-\Phi(\mathcal V,W,T\cap W)\leq -\epsilon.
\]
By Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:quotient-witness}, any realization of $(\mathcal V,U,T)$ gives a realization of the quotient profile and quotient flag associated with $W$.  By the first-moment upper bound in Corollary~\ref{qlcl:cor:one-flag-expectation} and Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:minor-potential}, the probability that this quotient realization exists is at most
\[
       q^{\Phi(\mathcal V,U,T)-\Phi(\mathcal V,W,T\cap W)}\leq q^{-\epsilon}.
\]
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:lem:pair-submodularity}
Let $U, \Omega, W, \Theta, T, T'$ be as defined above.
Then
\begin{equation}\label{qlcl:eq:pair-submod}
       \Phi^{(2)}(\mathcal V,\Omega,\Theta)
       \leq
       \Phi_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)
       +\Phi_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,W,T').
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Denote $V' = V_i \oplus V_i$. By rank-nullity
\[
    \dim (\Omega \cap V') = \dim \pi_1(V') + \dim (V' \cap \ker \pi_1).
\]
Because $\pi_1$ is a projection, $\pi_1(V')$ is contained in $V_i \cap U$, hence $\dim \pi_1(V') \le \dim (V_i \cap U)$.
Moreover, because $\pi_1$ is a projection to the first copy, we have:
\[
    V' \cap \ker \pi_1 \cong 0 \oplus (V_i \cap W).
\]
Hence, 
\[
       \dim((V_i\oplus V_i)\cap\Omega)
       \leq \dim(V_i\cap U)+\dim(V_i\cap W).
\]

Summing over $i$ gives $a_\mathcal V^{(2)}(\Omega)\leq a_\mathcal V(U)+a_\mathcal V(W)$.  Since $\pi_1$ is onto,
\[
       \dim\Omega=\dim U+\dim W,
       \qquad
       \dim\Theta=\dim T+\dim T'.
\]
Substitution into the doubled potential gives \eqref{qlcl:eq:pair-submod}.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:lem:dependent-pairs}
Assume $U\neq0$, $T\leq U$, $t=\dim T\leq c$, and
\[
       \Gamma_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)\geq\epsilon .
\]
Let $Y$ be the contribution to $\operatorname{\mathbb{E}} [X^2]$ from ordered pairs $(A,B)$ for which the joint row span of the concatenated matrix $[A\;B]$ is not $U\oplus U$.  Then
\[
       Y\leq q^{2\Phi_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)-\epsilon+8b^2}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Fix a joint row space $\Omega\leq U\oplus U$ whose two coordinate projections are $U$ and with $\Omega\neq U\oplus U$.  The number of ordered pairs $(A,B)$ satisfying the profile and having exact joint row span $\Omega$ is at most $q^{a_\mathcal V^{(2)}(\Omega)}$.

If both $A$ and $B$ are counted by $X$, then for $J=[A\;B]$ the joint logical row space $\Theta=\Lambda_S(J)$ satisfies $\Theta\leq\Omega$ and its two coordinate projections are both $T$.  For a subspace $L\leq \mathbb F_q^b \oplus \mathbb F_q^b $ we have the elementary identity
\[
       \pi_1(L^\perp)=\bigl(L\cap (\mathbb F_q^b \oplus 0)\bigr)^\perp,
\]
where $(L\cap (\mathbb F_q^b \oplus 0)\bigr)$ is identified in the natural manner with a subspace of $\mathbb F_q^b $, upon which the orthogonal complement is taken inside $\mathbb F_q^b $.  Applying it with $L=K_S(J)=\Lambda_S(J)^\perp$ gives
\[
       \pi_1(\Theta)=\bigl(K_S(J)\cap(\mathbb F_q^b\oplus0)\bigr)^\perp=K_S(A)^\perp=T,
\]
and similarly $\pi_2(\Theta)=T$.

For fixed $\Omega$ and $\Theta$, Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:fixed-matrix-prob} applied to $J$ gives the upper bound
\[
       q^{-a\dim\Omega-c(\dim\Omega-\dim\Theta)}
\]
for the probability of the corresponding joint event; we drop the injectivity factor.  There are at most $q^{4b^2}$ choices of $\Omega$ and at most $q^{4b^2}$ choices of $\Theta$.

Since $\Omega\neq U\oplus U$ and the first projection is onto, $W=\phi(\ker(\pi_1|_\Omega))$ is a proper subspace of $U$.  Moreover, if $T'=\phi(\ker(\pi_1|_\Theta))$, then $T'\leq T\cap W$, because the second projection of $\Theta$ is $T$.  Since the potential is monotone nondecreasing in the logical row space for fixed ordinary row space,
\[
       \Phi(\mathcal V,W,T')\leq \Phi(\mathcal V,W,T\cap W).
\]
The gap assumption gives
\[
       \Phi(\mathcal V,W,T')\leq \Phi(\mathcal V,U,T)-\epsilon.
\]
Applying Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:pair-submodularity}, we get that every joint type contributes at most
\[
       q^{\Phi^{(2)}(\mathcal V,\Omega,\Theta)}
       \leq q^{2\Phi(\mathcal V,U,T)-\epsilon}.
\]
Multiplying by the number of joint types proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:prop:fixed-supercritical}
Assume $U\neq0$, $T\leq U$, $t=\dim T\leq c$, and
\[
       \Gamma_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)\geq\epsilon.
\]
If $\epsilon\geq 2b^2+1$, then
\[
       \operatorname{Pr}[(S,C)\text{ realizes }(\mathcal V,U,T)]
       \geq 1-q^{-\epsilon+12b^2}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Let $X=X_{\mathcal V,U,T}$.  Because $0<U$ is one of the quotient minors, the gap assumption implies
\[
       \Phi(\mathcal V,U,T)\geq \epsilon.
\]
Corollary~\ref{qlcl:cor:one-flag-expectation} gives
\[
       \operatorname{\mathbb{E}} X\geq q^{\Phi(\mathcal V,U,T)-2b^2}.
\]

For ordered pairs $(A,B)$ with joint row span $U\oplus U$, the column spaces generated by $A$ and $B$ are independent subspaces of $\mathbb F_q^n$.  The restrictions of the random parity checks to these two subspaces are independent, so the covariance of the two indicator variables is zero.  For all remaining ordered pairs, the covariance is at most the joint probability, and Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:dependent-pairs} bounds the sum of these joint probabilities.  Therefore
\[
       \operatorname{Var}(X)
       \leq q^{2\Phi(\mathcal V,U,T)-\epsilon+8b^2}.
\]
Chebyshev's inequality yields
\[
       \operatorname{Pr}[X=0]
       \leq \frac{\operatorname{Var}(X)}{(\operatorname{\mathbb{E}} X)^2}
       \leq q^{-\epsilon+12b^2}.
\]
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:thm:fixed-type}
Let $(S,C)\sim\operatorname{\mathsf{PCSS}}(n,q;m_0,m_1)$.  Fix a $b$-local profile $\mathcal V$ and a flag $(U,T)$ with $U\neq0$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item If $\Gamma_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)\leq-\epsilon$, then
\[
       \operatorname{Pr}[(S,C)\text{ realizes }(\mathcal V,U,T)]\leq q^{-\epsilon}.
\]
\item If $\dim T\leq m_1-m_0$, $\Gamma_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal V,U,T)\geq\epsilon$, and $\epsilon\geq 2b^2+1$, then
\[
       \operatorname{Pr}[(S,C)\text{ realizes }(\mathcal V,U,T)]
       \geq 1-q^{-\epsilon+12b^2}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Part (a) is Proposition~\ref{qlcl:prop:fixed-subcritical}.  Part (b) is Proposition~\ref{qlcl:prop:fixed-supercritical}.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:thm:qlcl-threshold}
Let $(S,C)\sim\operatorname{\mathsf{PCSS}}(n,q;m_0,m_1)$ and let $\mathcal P(\mathcal F,\mathcal D)$ be a $b$-quotient LCL property with finite profile family $\mathcal F$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item \textbf{Subcritical region.}  If
\[
       \Gamma^{\max}_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal F,\mathcal D)
       \leq -\epsilon,
\]
then
\[
       \operatorname{Pr}[(S,C)\text{ satisfies }\mathcal P(\mathcal F,\mathcal D)]
       \leq |\mathcal F|\,q^{-\epsilon+2b^2}.
\]
\item \textbf{Supercritical region.}  If
\[
       \Gamma^{\max}_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal F,\mathcal D)
       \geq \epsilon
       \qquad\text{and}\qquad
       \epsilon\geq 2b^2+1,
\]
then
\[
       \operatorname{Pr}[(S,C)\text{ satisfies }\mathcal P(\mathcal F,\mathcal D)]
       \geq 1-q^{-\epsilon+12b^2}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
For (a), if the property holds then some flag $(U,T)$ and some profile $\mathcal V\in\mathcal F$ are realized, and any realized flag is parity-feasible: when $\dim T>m_1-m_0$, the realization probability vanishes by Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:fixed-matrix-prob}, since $\iota(c,t)=0$ for $t>c$.  The number of flags in $\mathbb F_q^b$ is at most $q^{2b^2}$.  Apply Theorem~\ref{qlcl:thm:fixed-type}(a) to each parity-feasible flag and union bound.

For (b), choose a profile and feasible flag attaining gap at least $\epsilon$.  Theorem~\ref{qlcl:thm:fixed-type}(b) implies that this one flagged profile is realized with probability at least $1-q^{-\epsilon+12b^2}$, and that realization witnesses $\mathcal P(\mathcal F,\mathcal D)$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- definition-18: body_md -->
Let $\operatorname{\mathsf{Nest}}(n,q;m_0,m_1)$ be the uniform distribution over all nested pairs
\[
       S\subseteq C\subseteq\mathbb F_q^n,
       \qquad
       \dim S=m_0,
       \qquad
       \dim C=m_1 .
\]
<!-- end definition-18 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:lem:conditioning}
Let
\[
       H=\begin{bmatrix}H_C\\ H_S\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Conditioned on the event that $H_C$ and $H$ have full row rank, $\operatorname{\mathsf{PCSS}}(n,q;m_0,m_1)$ is distributed as $\operatorname{\mathsf{Nest}}(n,q;m_0,m_1)$.  Moreover this full-rank event has probability at least
\[
       \gamma_q=\prod_{j=1}^{\infty}(1-q^{-j})^2>0.
\]
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
A uniformly random full-rank parity-check matrix $H_C\in\mathbb F_q^{a\times n}$ has a uniformly random kernel of dimension $m_1$.  Conditional on $C=\ker H_C$, the additional checks $H_S$ induce a uniformly random linear map $C\to\mathbb F_q^c$.  Conditional on this induced map having rank $c$, its kernel is a uniformly random $m_0$-dimensional subspace of $C$.  This is exactly the uniform nested ensemble.

The probability that a random $r\times N$ matrix over $\mathbb F_q$ has full row rank is $\prod_{j=N-r+1}^{N}(1-q^{-j})$, which is at least $\prod_{j=1}^{\infty}(1-q^{-j})$.  Apply this once to $H_C$ and once to the induced map on $C$.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:thm:uniform-threshold}
Let $(S,C)\sim\operatorname{\mathsf{Nest}}(n,q;m_0,m_1)$ and let $\mathcal P(\mathcal F,\mathcal D)$ be a $b$-quotient LCL property with $\mathcal F$ finite.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item \textbf{Subcritical region.}  If
\[
       \Gamma^{\max,\mathrm{unif}}_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal F,\mathcal D)\leq -\epsilon,
\]
then
\[
       \operatorname{Pr}[(S,C)\text{ satisfies }\mathcal P(\mathcal F,\mathcal D)]
       \leq \gamma_q^{-1}|\mathcal F|\,q^{-\epsilon+2b^2}.
\]
\item \textbf{Supercritical region.}  If
\[
       \Gamma^{\max,\mathrm{unif}}_{m_0,m_1}(\mathcal F,\mathcal D)\geq \epsilon
       \qquad\text{and}\qquad
       \epsilon\geq 2b^2+1,
\]
then
\[
       \operatorname{Pr}[(S,C)\text{ satisfies }\mathcal P(\mathcal F,\mathcal D)]
       \geq 1-\gamma_q^{-1}q^{-\epsilon+12b^2}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Let $\mathcal R$ be the full-rank event from Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:conditioning}.  Conditional on $\mathcal R$, the parity-check ensemble is the uniform nested ensemble.

For (a), if the property holds in a deterministic nested pair of dimensions $(m_0,m_1)$, Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:auto-feasibility} implies that some feasible flag in the indexing set of \eqref{qlcl:eq:Gmax-unif} is realized.  The number of flags in $\mathbb F_q^b$ is at most $q^{2b^2}$.  Theorem~\ref{qlcl:thm:fixed-type}(a), applied in the parity-check ensemble and union bounded over feasible flags and profiles, gives unconditional probability at most $|\mathcal F|q^{-\epsilon+2b^2}$.  Conditioning on $\mathcal R$ multiplies this by at most $\gamma_q^{-1}$.

For (b), choose a feasible profile and flag attaining gap at least $\epsilon$.  Theorem~\ref{qlcl:thm:fixed-type}(b) gives probability at most $q^{-\epsilon+12b^2}$ that this flag is not realized in the parity-check ensemble.  Conditioning on $\mathcal R$ again multiplies the failure probability by at most $\gamma_q^{-1}$.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:lem:trace-pairing}
Let $D\leq\mathbb F_q^n$ be an $\mathbb F_q$-linear subspace and let $x\in\mathbb F_q^n$.  Then $X(x)$ commutes with $Z(z)$ for every $z\in D$ iff $x\in D^\perp$, where $D^\perp$ is the orthogonal complement with respect to the $\mathbb F_q$-bilinear form $\left\langle \cdot,\cdot\right\rangle$.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
If $x\in D^\perp$, then $\left\langle x,z\right\rangle=0$, hence $\operatorname{Tr}(\left\langle x,z\right\rangle)=0$, for every $z\in D$.  Conversely, suppose $\operatorname{Tr}(\left\langle x,z\right\rangle)=0$ for every $z\in D$, and fix $z\in D$.  Since $D$ is $\mathbb F_q$-linear, $cz\in D$ for every $c\in\mathbb F_q$, so $\operatorname{Tr}(c\left\langle x,z\right\rangle)=0$ for all $c\in\mathbb F_q$.  The trace form $(a,b)\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}(ab)$ is nondegenerate on $\mathbb F_q$ because the extension $\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p$ is separable, so $\left\langle x,z\right\rangle=0$.  As $z\in D$ was arbitrary, $x\in D^\perp$.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- definition-19: body_md -->
\label{qlcl:def:css-from-pair}
Given $S\subseteq C\subseteq\mathbb F_q^n$, define the CSS code $Q(S,C)$ whose $X$-type stabilizer labels are $S$ and whose $Z$-type stabilizer labels are $C^\perp$:
\[
       \mathsf S_X=S,
       \qquad
       \mathsf S_Z=C^\perp.
\]
By Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:trace-pairing}, every $X$-type stabilizer $X(x)$, $x\in S$, commutes with every $Z$-type stabilizer $Z(z)$, $z\in C^\perp$, iff $S\subseteq(C^\perp)^\perp=C$, which holds by hypothesis.  The number of encoded qudits is
\[
       k=n-\dim S-\dim C^\perp=\dim C-\dim S.
\]
<!-- end definition-19 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{obs:pos-of-d}
    For a subspace $W<U$,
    \[
        \kappa_s(U,T)-\kappa_s(W,T\cap W) \ge (n-m_1)(\dim U - \dim W) > 0.
    \]
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Write $d = \dim U - \dim W$, and $\ell = \dim W - \dim (T \cup W)$.
    \begin{align*}
        \kappa_s(U,T)-\kappa_s(W,T\cap W) &= (n-m_1^s)d + (m_1-m_0)(d-\ell) \\
        &\ge (n-m_1^s)d\\
        &>0.
    \end{align*}
    The first inequality follows because $d> \ell$, and the second is true because $d>0$, as $W$ is a strict subspace of $U$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- definition-20: body_md -->
\label{def:flagged-sop}
For $U\ne0$, $T\le U$, and $W<U$, define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:flagged-slope}
 \lambda_{s}(\mathcal V;U,T)
 :=\min_{W<U}
 \frac{a_{\mathcal V}(U)-a_{\mathcal V}(W)}
      {\kappa_s(U,T)-\kappa_s(W,T\cap W)}.
\end{equation}
Set $\lambda_{s}(\mathcal V;0,0):=+\infty$.
<!-- end definition-20 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:fixed-type}
Suppose a random nested pair has dimensions $(m_0^s,m_1^s)$. If a nonzero
flagged type $(\mathcal V, U ,T)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:lambda-low}
        \lambda_{s}(\mathcal V;U,T)\le1-\eta,
\end{equation}
then for $(S, C) \sim \operatorname{\mathsf{PCSS}}(n, q; m_0^s, m_1^s)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-type-input}
 \Pr[(S,C)\text{ realizes }(\mathcal V,U,T)]
 \le q^{-\eta(n-m_1^s)}.
\end{equation}
For the uniform exact-dimensional model, the same estimate holds up to the
standard constant full-rank conditioning factor.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Observe that \cref{eq:lambda-low} implies the existence of a subspace $W < U$ such that
    \begin{align*}
        a_{\mathcal V}(U)-a_{\mathcal V}(W) -(\kappa_s(U,T)-\kappa_s(W,T\cap W)) &\le -\eta \cdot (\kappa_s(U,T)-\kappa_s(W,T\cap W)) \\
        &\le -\eta \cdot (n-m^s_1).
    \end{align*}
    The second inequality follows from Lemma~\ref{obs:pos-of-d} and the fact that $\dim U -\dim W \ge 1$.
    Further, we see that $a_{\mathcal V}(U)-a_{\mathcal V}(W) -(\kappa_s(U,T)-\kappa_s(W,T\cap W)) \le -\eta \cdot (n-m_1^s)$ implies
    \[
        \Gamma_{m_0^s,m_1^s}(\mathcal V, U ,T) \le -\eta \cdot (n-m_1^s).
    \]
    Applying Proposition~\ref{qlcl:prop:fixed-subcritical} with the above bound, the proposition follows.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- definition-21: body_md -->
Upon denoting $r_s=m_1^s/n$, define:
\begin{equation}
    \label{eq:flagged-rate-score}
    R^{\mathrm{flag}}_{s}(\mathcal V;U,T)
    :=
    1-(1-r_s)\lambda_{s}(\mathcal V;U,T).
\end{equation}
<!-- end definition-21 -->
<!-- definition-22: body_md -->
\[
 R_{\rm cl}(\mathcal V;U)
 :=1-\min_{W<U}
 \frac{a_{\mathcal V}(U)-a_{\mathcal V}(W)}{n(\dim U-\dim W)}.
\]
<!-- end definition-22 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:sub-one-sector-comparison}
Every nonzero flag $T\le U$ satisfies
$R_s^{\rm flag}(\mathcal V;U,T)\ge R_{\rm cl}(\mathcal V;U)$, with equality for $T=U$.
Moreover, for every $W<U$,
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:sub-minor-rate-bound}
 a_{\mathcal V}(U)-a_{\mathcal V}(W)
 \ge n\bigl(1-R_s^{\rm flag}(\mathcal V;U,T)\bigr)(\dim U-\dim W).
\end{equation}
If $A$ realizes $(U,T)$, then $T=U$ iff
$\operatorname{im}(A)\cap S_s=\{0\}$.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
For $d:=\dim U-\dim W$ and
$\ell:=\dim T-\dim(T\cap W)$,
\[
 \kappa_s(U,T)-\kappa_s(W,T\cap W)
 =(n-m_1^s)d+(m_1^s-m_0^s)(d-\ell)
 \ge n(1-r_s)d.
\]
Combining this with \eqref{eq:flagged-rate-score} gives
\eqref{eq:sub-minor-rate-bound} and hence the threshold comparison.  For
$T=U$, one has $\ell=d$ for every minor, giving equality.  The last statement
is equivalent to equality of the logical and ordinary kernels.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{thm:sub-asymmetric-sector-reduction}
For every common-profile joint witness,
\[
 \boxed{
 R_{\rm cl}(\mathcal V;U_X+U_Z)
 \le
 \max\{R_X^{\rm flag}(\mathcal V;U_X,T_X),
       R_Z^{\rm flag}(\mathcal V;U_Z,T_Z)\}.}
\]
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Let $R_*$ be the larger marginal fixed-type threshold and fix
$W<U_X+U_Z$. Two applications of
\eqref{eq:sub-mass-supermodular} (first with $U_X, W$, and the second with $U_Z, W+U_X$) gives
\begin{align*}
 a_{\mathcal V}(U_X+U_Z)-a_{\mathcal V}(W)
 \ge{}&a_{\mathcal V}(U_X)-a_{\mathcal V}(U_X\cap W)\\
 &+a_{\mathcal V}(U_Z)-a_{\mathcal V}(U_Z\cap(W+U_X)).
\end{align*}
By Proposition~\ref{prop:sub-one-sector-comparison}, the right side is at
least
\[
 n(1-R_*)\bigl[\dim U_X-\dim(U_X\cap W)
 +\dim U_Z-\dim(U_Z\cap(W+U_X))\bigr].
\]
The bracket equals $\dim(U_X+U_Z)-\dim W$.  The definition of
$R_{\rm cl}(\mathcal V;U_X+U_Z)$ now gives the claim.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- definition-23: body_md -->
\label{def:join-realize}
    Let $C_X, C_Z$ and $S_X, S_Z$ be the normalizer and stabilizer labels for the two sectors of CSS code $C = Q(S_X, C_X)$.
    For subspaces $U_s, T_s$, and $\mathcal V$ as defined above, we say that $C$ \emph{jointly realizes} $(\mathcal V, U_X+U_Z, T_X+T_Z)$ if there exist matrices  $A_s \in \mathbb F_q^{n \times b}$ for $s \in \{X,Z\}$ such that:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item  all $i \in [n]$, the $i$th row of $A_s$ lies in $V_i$;
        \item $\operatorname{row}(A_s)=U_s$;
        \item every column of $A_s$ lies in $C_s$;
        \item $\Lambda_{S_s}(A_s) = T_s$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Such matrices $(A_X, A_Z)$ are called realizations of $(\mathcal V, U, T)$.
<!-- end definition-23 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{thm:sub-joint-sector-preservation}
For arbitrary sector parameters,
\[
   \boxed{R^{\rm joint}(\mathcal F)=R_{\rm cl}(\mathcal F).}
\]
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
Every subspace $U_X+U_Z$ is in $\operatorname{LDist}_b$ because it
contains $T_X+T_Z\in\operatorname{LDist}_b$.  Theorem~\ref{thm:sub-asymmetric-sector-reduction}
therefore gives $R_{\rm cl}(\mathcal F) \le R^{\rm joint}(\mathcal F)$.
Conversely, take the $(\mathcal V, U)$ that minimizes $R_{\rm cl}(\mathcal F)$ and choose $(U_X,T_X)=(U,U)$ and $(U_Z,T_Z)=(0,0)$.
Thus, $T_X+T_Z=U \in \operatorname{LDist}_b$, and we have that $\max\{R_X^{\rm flag}(\mathcal V;U_X,T_X), R_Z^{\rm flag}(\mathcal V;U_Z,T_Z)\} = R_X^{\rm flag}(\mathcal V;U,U)$, which is equal to $R_{\rm cl}(\mathcal V, U)$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:sub-one-sector-comparison}.
The theorem follows.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:joint-form}
For the event $E$ defined above, we have:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prob-join-sat}
    Pr_C[E(C, \mathcal F)] \le |\mathcal F|\cdot q^{4b^2} \cdot q^{-\delta n}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
The corollary follows by union bounding over all $\mathcal V \in \mathcal F$, $U_X,U_Z,T_X,T_Z$ satisfying the appropriate conditions, and then applying Proposition~\ref{prop:fixed-type}.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:list-dec-joint}
    Let $\mathcal F_{\rm LD}$ denote the family of local profiles associated with (the complement of) $(\rho, L)$-list decodability. Then,
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:list-dec-joint}
        R^{\rm joint}(\mathcal F_{\rm LD}) = R_{\rm cl}(\mathcal F_{\rm LD}) = 1-\frac{L+1}{L} \rho.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
This follows by combining \cref{thm:sub-joint-sector-preservation} with the list-decoding upper and lower bounds of \cite{AGL24, LMS25}.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:list-rec-joint}
    Let $\mathcal F_{\rm LR}$ denote the family of local profiles associated with (the complement of) $(\rho, \ell, L)$-list recoverability. Then, if for $\varepsilon>0$, $\rho, \ell, L$ satisfy
    \[
        L \le \left( \frac{\ell}{1-\rho}\right)^{(1-\rho)/\varepsilon}
    \]
    then
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:list-rec-joint}
        R^{\rm joint}(\mathcal F_{\rm LR}) = R_{\rm cl}(\mathcal F_{\rm LR}) \ge  1-\rho-\varepsilon.
    \end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
This follows by combining \cref{thm:sub-joint-sector-preservation} with the list-recovery bound in \cite{GG26}, where they proved that random linear codes of rate $R$ achieve $(1-R-\varepsilon, \ell, (\ell/(R+\varepsilon))^{(R+\varepsilon)/\varepsilon})$-list recoverability.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{rsd:rem:trace-pairing-folded}
As in the scalar case (Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:trace-pairing}), the commutation phase of a pair of generalized Pauli operators over \(\mathbb F_q\), \(q=p^e\), is the additive character \(\omega_p^{\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p}(\cdot)}\) applied to the \(\mathbb F_q\)-valued pairing.  Concretely, choose an \(\mathbb F_q\)-basis of \(W\) identifying the fixed nondegenerate form \(\left\langle \cdot,\cdot\right\rangle_W\) with the standard form on \(\mathbb F_q^s\); each folded coordinate is then a block of \(s\) qudits, and \(X(x)\) commutes with \(Z(z)\) iff \(\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p}(\left\langle x,z\right\rangle)=0\), where \(\left\langle \cdot,\cdot\right\rangle\) is the coordinatewise extension of \(\left\langle \cdot,\cdot\right\rangle_W\).  For an individual pair of vectors this trace condition is strictly weaker than \(\left\langle x,z\right\rangle=0\) when \(q\) is not prime.  For \(\mathbb F_q\)-linear subspaces the two conditions coincide: every code space in this paper is \(\mathbb F_q\)-linear, hence closed under scalar multiplication, so \(X(x)\) commutes with all of \(\{Z(z):z\in D\}\) iff \(x\in D^\perp\), by the argument of Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:trace-pairing} applied verbatim to the pairing on \(W^n\).  All CSS commutation requirements below are of this subspace form, so the \(\mathbb F_q\)-bilinear model used throughout is faithful to physical Pauli commutation; the \(\mathbb F_q\)-valued pairing should not be read as an individual-pair commutation criterion.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rsd:rem:folded-metric}
All subspace-design and distance statements in the folded part of the paper use the block metric on the coordinates of \(W^n\).  If \(W=\mathbb F_q^s\) is unfolded into scalar coordinates, the scalar length becomes \(ns\).  A block-weight lower bound \(\operatorname{wt}_{\rm block}(x)\ge \delta n\) implies scalar weight at least \(\delta n\), and hence scalar relative distance at least \(\delta/s\), but not necessarily \(\delta\).  Thus the construction obtained later is binary in the folded sense: it is a CSS code over a constant-dimensional binary vector alphabet, with Singleton-scale guarantees in the folded metric.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
A symmetric CSS pair is obtained from \(S=N^\perp\subseteq N\).  Then \(C_2=S\) and \(C_1=N\), the two logical sectors are naturally dual copies of \(N/S\), and the quantum rate is \((2\dim N-ns)/(ns)\).  The general nested-pair formulation below includes this case but is more convenient for the probabilistic inner-code construction.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- definition-24: body_md -->
\label{rsd:def:folded-ensembles}
Fix a basis of \(W\), identifying \(W^n\) with \(\mathbb F_q^{ns}\), and put
\[
   a=ns-m_1,
   \qquad
   c=m_1-m_0 .
\]
The folded parity-check ensemble \(\operatorname{\mathsf{PCSS}}^W(n,q;m_0,m_1)\) samples independent uniform matrices \(H_C\in\mathbb F_q^{a\times ns}\) and \(H_S\in\mathbb F_q^{c\times ns}\) and sets \(N=\ker H_C\) and \(S=\ker H_C\cap\ker H_S\); this is exactly \(\operatorname{\mathsf{PCSS}}(ns,q;m_0,m_1)\) of Definition~\ref{qlcl:def:pcss} on the scalar unfolding.  The folded uniform ensemble \(\operatorname{\mathsf{Nest}}^W(n,q;m_0,m_1)\) is likewise \(\operatorname{\mathsf{Nest}}(ns,q;m_0,m_1)\).  The folded flag cost is
\[
   \kappa^W_{m_0,m_1}(U,T)
      \coloneqq au+c(u-t)
      =(ns-m_0)(u-t)+(ns-m_1)t,
\]
so that \(\Phi^W_{m_0,m_1}(\mathfrak V,U,T)=a_{\mathfrak V}(U)-\kappa^W_{m_0,m_1}(U,T)\) in~\eqref{eq:folded-qlcl-potential}.
<!-- end definition-24 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{rsd:lem:folded-exact-count}
Let \(\mathfrak V\) be a folded local profile and \(U\le B^*\).  Then \(|\mathcal M^{=}_{\mathfrak V}(U)|\le q^{a_{\mathfrak V}(U)}\).  Moreover, if
\[
   a_{\mathfrak V}(U)-a_{\mathfrak V}(U')\ge\epsilon
   \qquad\text{for every proper }U'<U,
\]
then
\[
   |\mathcal M^{=}_{\mathfrak V}(U)|
      \ge q^{a_{\mathfrak V}(U)}\bigl(1-q^{-\epsilon+b^2}\bigr).
\]
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
The upper bound is~\eqref{eq:folded-mass-count}.  A map in \(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak V}(U)\) whose row space is not \(U\) lies in \(\mathcal M_{\mathfrak V}(U')\) for some proper \(U'<U\).  The number of subspaces of \(B^*\cong\mathbb F_q^b\) is at most \(q^{b^2}\), so
\[
   |\mathcal M_{\mathfrak V}(U)\setminus\mathcal M^{=}_{\mathfrak V}(U)|
      \le\sum_{U'<U}q^{a_{\mathfrak V}(U')}
      \le q^{b^2}\,q^{a_{\mathfrak V}(U)-\epsilon}.
\]
Subtracting from~\eqref{eq:folded-mass-count} proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{rsd:lem:folded-fixed-map}
Let \(M:B\to W^n\) have \(\operatorname{row}(M)=U\), \(\dim U=u\), and let \(T\le U\), \(\dim T=t\).  In the ensemble \(\operatorname{\mathsf{PCSS}}^W(n,q;m_0,m_1)\),
\[
   \operatorname{Pr}\bigl[M(B)\subseteq N\text{ and }\Lambda_S(M)=T\bigr]
      =q^{-\kappa^W_{m_0,m_1}(U,T)}\,\iota(c,t),
\]
with \(\iota(c,t)\) as in Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:fixed-matrix-prob}.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Under the identification \(W^n\cong\mathbb F_q^{ns}\), the map \(M\) is a linear map \(B\to\mathbb F_q^{ns}\) with \(\ker M=U^\circ\), so \(\dim M(B)=u\).  The event \(M(B)\subseteq N\) is \(H_CM=0\), which constrains each of the \(a\) rows of \(H_C\) to lie in the codimension-\(u\) space \(M(B)^\perp\); it has probability \(q^{-au}\) and depends only on \(H_C\).

Condition on \(H_CM=0\).  Then \(K_S(M)=M^{-1}(S)=\ker(H_SM)\), and \(\Lambda_S(M)=T\) iff \(\ker(H_SM)=T^\circ\).  Since \(H_S\) is uniform and independent of \(H_C\), the map induced by \(H_SM\) on \(B/\ker M\) is a uniformly random linear map from a \(u\)-dimensional space to \(\mathbb F_q^c\).  As \(U^\circ=\ker M\subseteq T^\circ\), the condition \(\ker(H_SM)=T^\circ\) says that this random map vanishes exactly on the fixed \((u-t)\)-dimensional subspace \(T^\circ/U^\circ\): vanishing on it has probability \(q^{-c(u-t)}\), and after quotienting by it, injectivity of the induced map on the remaining \(t\)-dimensional space has probability \(\iota(c,t)\).  Multiplying the factors gives the claim, since \(au+c(u-t)=\kappa^W_{m_0,m_1}(U,T)\).
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{rsd:cor:folded-one-flag}
Let
\[
   X^W_{\mathfrak V,U,T}
      =\#\{M\in\mathcal M^{=}_{\mathfrak V}(U):\ M(B)\subseteq N,\ \Lambda_S(M)=T\}.
\]
Then
\[
   \operatorname{\mathbb{E}} X^W_{\mathfrak V,U,T}\le q^{\Phi^W_{m_0,m_1}(\mathfrak V,U,T)}.
\]
If \(\Gamma^W_{m_0,m_1}(\mathfrak V,U,T)\ge\epsilon\), \(t\le c\), and \(\epsilon\ge2b^2+1\), then
\[
   \operatorname{\mathbb{E}} X^W_{\mathfrak V,U,T}\ge q^{\Phi^W_{m_0,m_1}(\mathfrak V,U,T)-2b^2}.
\]
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
Combine Lemmas~\ref{rsd:lem:folded-exact-count} and~\ref{rsd:lem:folded-fixed-map} with~\eqref{eq:folded-gamma-mass}, exactly as in Corollary~\ref{qlcl:cor:one-flag-expectation}: the upper bound uses \(|\mathcal M^{=}_{\mathfrak V}(U)|\le q^{a_{\mathfrak V}(U)}\); the lower bound uses \(|\mathcal M^{=}_{\mathfrak V}(U)|\ge q^{a_{\mathfrak V}(U)}(1-q^{-\epsilon+b^2})\) together with \(\iota(c,t)\ge q^{-t}\ge q^{-b}\) for \(t\le c\) and \(1-q^{-\epsilon+b^2}\ge q^{-1}\) under the numerical assumption.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{rsd:lem:folded-minor}
Let \(U_0<U\le B^*\), let \(\rho:U\to\overline U=U/U_0\) be the quotient map, and let \(\overline B\) be a coefficient space of dimension \(\dim\overline U\) with a fixed identification \(\overline B^*\cong\overline U\).  There is a linear map \(\beta:\overline B\to B\) with \(\beta^*|_U=\rho\).  Define the quotient folded profile
\[
   \overline{\mathfrak V}_i
      =\{f\circ\beta:\ f\in\mathfrak V_i\cap\operatorname{Hom}_U(B,W)\}
      \le\operatorname{Hom}(\overline B,W).
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If \(M\) is a folded realization of \((\mathfrak V,U,T)\) in \(S\subseteq N\), then \(\overline M=M\circ\beta\) is a folded realization of \((\overline{\mathfrak V},\overline U,\rho(T))\) in the same nested pair, and \(\dim\rho(T)=\dim T-\dim(T\cap U_0)\).
\item \(a_{\overline{\mathfrak V}}(\overline U)=a_{\mathfrak V}(U)-a_{\mathfrak V}(U_0)\).
\item \(\Phi^W_{m_0,m_1}(\overline{\mathfrak V},\overline U,\rho(T))
        =\Phi^W_{m_0,m_1}(\mathfrak V,U,T)
        -\Phi^W_{m_0,m_1}(\mathfrak V,U_0,T\cap U_0)\).
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Existence of \(\beta\): extend \(\rho\), viewed through the identification \(\overline U\cong\overline B^*\) as a map \(U\to\overline B^*\), to a linear map \(B^*\to\overline B^*\), and let \(\beta\) be its dual.

Throughout we use the standard annihilator identity: for a linear map \(\beta:\overline B\to B\) and a subspace \(K\le B\),
\[
   (\beta^{-1}K)^\circ=\beta^*(K^\circ)\le\overline B^* .
\]
(The inclusion \(\supseteq\) is direct; equality follows from the dimension count
\(\dim(\beta^{-1}K)^\circ
   =\dim\operatorname{im}\beta-\dim(K\cap\operatorname{im}\beta)
   =\dim\beta^*(K^\circ)\).)

(i)  Since \(\operatorname{row}(M)=U\), we have \(\ker M=U^\circ\subseteq\ker M_i\), so \(M_i\in\mathfrak V_i\cap\operatorname{Hom}_U(B,W)\) and hence \(\overline M_i=M_i\circ\beta\in\overline{\mathfrak V}_i\) for every \(i\).  The image of \(\overline M\) is contained in \(M(B)\subseteq N\).  For the row space, \(\ker\overline M=\beta^{-1}(\ker M)=\beta^{-1}(U^\circ)\), so by the annihilator identity \(\operatorname{row}(\overline M)=\beta^*(U)=\rho(U)=\overline U\).  For the logical row space, \(K_S(\overline M)=\beta^{-1}(K_S(M))=\beta^{-1}(T^\circ)\), hence \(\Lambda_S(\overline M)=\beta^*(T)=\rho(T)\), using \(T\le U\) and \(\beta^*|_U=\rho\).  The kernel of \(\rho|_T\) is \(T\cap U_0\), which gives the dimension formula.

(ii)  Fix \(i\) and consider the surjective linear map \(f\mapsto f\circ\beta\) from \(\mathfrak V_i\cap\operatorname{Hom}_U(B,W)\) onto \(\overline{\mathfrak V}_i\).  Its kernel consists of those \(f\) that vanish on \(U^\circ+\operatorname{im}\beta\).  Now
\[
   (U^\circ+\operatorname{im}\beta)^\circ
      =U\cap(\operatorname{im}\beta)^\circ
      =U\cap\ker\beta^*
      =\ker(\beta^*|_U)
      =\ker\rho
      =U_0,
\]
so \(U^\circ+\operatorname{im}\beta=U_0^\circ\), and the kernel is exactly \(\mathfrak V_i\cap\operatorname{Hom}_{U_0}(B,W)\).  Rank--nullity gives
\[
   \dim\overline{\mathfrak V}_i
      =\dim\bigl(\mathfrak V_i\cap\operatorname{Hom}_U(B,W)\bigr)
      -\dim\bigl(\mathfrak V_i\cap\operatorname{Hom}_{U_0}(B,W)\bigr).
\]
Since \(\overline U=\overline B^*\) is the full dual space, \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\overline U}(\overline B,W)=\operatorname{Hom}(\overline B,W)\), so \(a_{\overline{\mathfrak V}}(\overline U)=\sum_i\dim\overline{\mathfrak V}_i\), and summing the display over \(i\) proves (ii).

(iii)  By (i), \(\dim\overline U=u-\dim U_0\) and \(\dim\rho(T)=t-\dim(T\cap U_0)\), so the second expression for \(\kappa^W\) in Definition~\ref{rsd:def:folded-ensembles} gives
\[
   \kappa^W_{m_0,m_1}(\overline U,\rho(T))
      =\kappa^W_{m_0,m_1}(U,T)-\kappa^W_{m_0,m_1}(U_0,T\cap U_0).
\]
Combining with (ii) proves (iii).
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{rsd:prop:folded-subcritical}
If \(U\neq0\), \(T\le U\), and \(\Gamma^W_{m_0,m_1}(\mathfrak V,U,T)\le-\epsilon\), then, for \((S,N)\sim\operatorname{\mathsf{PCSS}}^W(n,q;m_0,m_1)\),
\[
   \operatorname{Pr}\bigl[(S,N)\text{ admits a folded realization of }(\mathfrak V,U,T)\bigr]
      \le q^{-\epsilon}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Choose \(U_0<U\) with \(\Phi^W(\mathfrak V,U,T)-\Phi^W(\mathfrak V,U_0,T\cap U_0)\le-\epsilon\).  By Lemma~\ref{rsd:lem:folded-minor}(i), any realization of \((\mathfrak V,U,T)\) yields a realization of \((\overline{\mathfrak V},\overline U,\rho(T))\) in the same pair.  By Markov's inequality, the first-moment upper bound of Corollary~\ref{rsd:cor:folded-one-flag} applied to the quotient data, and Lemma~\ref{rsd:lem:folded-minor}(iii), this quotient realization exists with probability at most
\[
   q^{\Phi^W(\overline{\mathfrak V},\overline U,\rho(T))}
      =q^{\Phi^W(\mathfrak V,U,T)-\Phi^W(\mathfrak V,U_0,T\cap U_0)}
      \le q^{-\epsilon}. \qedhere
\]
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{rsd:lem:folded-pair-submodularity}
Let \(\Omega\le U\oplus U\) and suppose the first projection \(\pi_1:\Omega\to U\) is onto.  Identify \(U_0=\ker(\pi_1|_\Omega)\) with a subspace of the second copy of \(U\).  Let \(\Theta\le\Omega\) satisfy \(\pi_1(\Theta)=T\), and put \(T'=\ker(\pi_1|_\Theta)\), so that \(T'\le U_0\) because \(\Theta\le\Omega\).  Then
\[
   \Phi^{(2),W}(\mathfrak V,\Omega,\Theta)
      \le\Phi^W_{m_0,m_1}(\mathfrak V,U,T)
      +\Phi^W_{m_0,m_1}(\mathfrak V,U_0,T').
\]
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
We use the standard duality for a subspace \(L\le B\oplus B\): the annihilator of \(\pi_2(L)\) inside \(B^*\) equals \(\{\psi\in B^*:(0,\psi)\in L^\circ\}\), and dually \(\pi_1(L^\circ)=\bigl(L\cap(B\oplus0)\bigr)^\circ\), the annihilator taken inside the first factor.

Fix a coordinate \(i\) and let \(h=(f,g)\in(\mathfrak V_i\oplus\mathfrak V_i)\cap\operatorname{Hom}_\Omega(B\oplus B,W)\), so that \(\Omega^\circ\subseteq\ker h\) inside \(B\oplus B\).

First, \(f\in\mathfrak V_i\cap\operatorname{Hom}_U(B,W)\): for \(x\in U^\circ\) and every \((\phi,\psi)\in\Omega\le U\oplus U\) one has \(\phi(x)+\psi(0)=0\), so \((x,0)\in\Omega^\circ\) and hence \(f(x)=h(x,0)=0\).  Thus \(h\mapsto f\) is a linear map into \(\mathfrak V_i\cap\operatorname{Hom}_U(B,W)\).

Second, the kernel of this map consists of pairs \((0,g)\) with \(g\) vanishing on \(\pi_2(\Omega^\circ)\).  By the duality above applied to \(L=\Omega^\circ\), the annihilator of \(\pi_2(\Omega^\circ)\) is \(\{\psi:(0,\psi)\in\Omega\}=\ker(\pi_1|_\Omega)=U_0\), so \(\pi_2(\Omega^\circ)=U_0^\circ\) and \(g\in\mathfrak V_i\cap\operatorname{Hom}_{U_0}(B,W)\).  Rank--nullity gives
\[
   \dim\bigl((\mathfrak V_i\oplus\mathfrak V_i)\cap\operatorname{Hom}_\Omega(B\oplus B,W)\bigr)
      \le\dim\bigl(\mathfrak V_i\cap\operatorname{Hom}_U(B,W)\bigr)
      +\dim\bigl(\mathfrak V_i\cap\operatorname{Hom}_{U_0}(B,W)\bigr).
\]
Summing over \(i\) yields \(a^{(2)}_{\mathfrak V}(\Omega)\le a_{\mathfrak V}(U)+a_{\mathfrak V}(U_0)\).  Since \(\pi_1|_\Omega\) is onto with kernel \(U_0\) and \(\pi_1(\Theta)=T\) with kernel \(T'\),
\[
   \dim\Omega=\dim U+\dim U_0,
   \qquad
   \dim\Theta=\dim T+\dim T',
\]
and substituting into the joint potential proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{rsd:lem:folded-dependent-pairs}
Assume \(U\neq0\), \(T\le U\), \(t\le c\), and \(\Gamma^W_{m_0,m_1}(\mathfrak V,U,T)\ge\epsilon\).  Let \(Y\) be the contribution to \(\operatorname{\mathbb{E}}\bigl[(X^W_{\mathfrak V,U,T})^2\bigr]\) from ordered pairs \((M,M')\) for which the joint map \(J:B\oplus B\to W^n\), \(J(x,y)=M(x)+M'(y)\), has \(row(J)\neq U\oplus U\).  Then
\[
   Y\le q^{2\Phi^W_{m_0,m_1}(\mathfrak V,U,T)-\epsilon+8b^2}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
If \(\operatorname{row}(M)=\operatorname{row}(M')=U\), then \(\ker J\supseteq\ker M\oplus\ker M'\) gives \(\Omega\coloneqq row(J)\le U\oplus U\), and
\(\pi_1(\Omega)^\circ=\{x:(x,0)\in\ker J\}=\ker M=U^\circ\),
so \(\pi_1(\Omega)=U\); similarly \(\pi_2(\Omega)=U\).  Fix such a joint row space \(\Omega\neq U\oplus U\).  The coordinates of \(J\) are \(J_i=(M_i,M'_i)\in(\mathfrak V_i\oplus\mathfrak V_i)\cap\operatorname{Hom}_\Omega(B\oplus B,W)\), so the number of ordered pairs with exact joint row space \(\Omega\) is at most \(q^{a^{(2)}_{\mathfrak V}(\Omega)}\).

If both \(M\) and \(M'\) are counted by \(X^W_{\mathfrak V,U,T}\), then the joint logical row space \(\Theta=\Lambda_S(J)\le\Omega\) has both projections equal to \(T\): by the duality of Lemma~\ref{rsd:lem:folded-pair-submodularity} applied to \(L=K_S(J)\), and since \(K_S(J)\cap(B\oplus0)=K_S(M)\oplus0\),
\[
   \pi_1(\Theta)
      =\pi_1\bigl(K_S(J)^\circ\bigr)
      =\bigl(K_S(J)\cap(B\oplus0)\bigr)^\circ
      =K_S(M)^\circ=T,
\]
and similarly \(\pi_2(\Theta)=T\).  For fixed \((\Omega,\Theta)\), Lemma~\ref{rsd:lem:folded-fixed-map} applied to \(J\) bounds the probability of the corresponding joint event by \(q^{-a\dim\Omega-c(\dim\Omega-\dim\Theta)}\), dropping the injectivity factor.  The number of choices of \(\Omega\) and of \(\Theta\) in \(B^*\oplus B^*\) is at most \(q^{4b^2}\) each.

Apply Lemma~\ref{rsd:lem:folded-pair-submodularity}.  Since \(\Omega\neq U\oplus U\) and \(\pi_1|_\Omega\) is onto, \(U_0=\ker(\pi_1|_\Omega)\) is a proper subspace of \(U\).  Moreover \(T'=\ker(\pi_1|_\Theta)\le T\cap U_0\), because the second projection of \(\Theta\) is \(T\).  The potential is monotone nondecreasing in the logical row space for fixed ordinary row space, since its coefficient on \(\dim T\) is \(c\ge0\); hence
\[
   \Phi^W(\mathfrak V,U_0,T')
      \le\Phi^W(\mathfrak V,U_0,T\cap U_0)
      \le\Phi^W(\mathfrak V,U,T)-\epsilon,
\]
using the gap assumption in the last step.  Therefore every joint type contributes at most
\[
   q^{\Phi^{(2),W}(\mathfrak V,\Omega,\Theta)}
      \le q^{2\Phi^W(\mathfrak V,U,T)-\epsilon},
\]
and multiplying by the at most \(q^{8b^2}\) joint types proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
\label{rsd:thm:folded-fixed-type}
Let \((S,N)\sim\operatorname{\mathsf{PCSS}}^W(n,q;m_0,m_1)\).  Fix a folded local profile \(\mathfrak V\) and a flag \((U,T)\) with \(U\neq0\), \(T\le U\le B^*\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item If \(\Gamma^W_{m_0,m_1}(\mathfrak V,U,T)\le-\epsilon\), then
\[
   \operatorname{Pr}\bigl[(S,N)\text{ admits a folded realization of }(\mathfrak V,U,T)\bigr]\le q^{-\epsilon}.
\]
\item If \(\dim T\le m_1-m_0\), \(\Gamma^W_{m_0,m_1}(\mathfrak V,U,T)\ge\epsilon\), and \(\epsilon\ge2b^2+1\), then
\[
   \operatorname{Pr}\bigl[(S,N)\text{ admits a folded realization of }(\mathfrak V,U,T)\bigr]
      \ge1-q^{-\epsilon+12b^2}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
In particular, Theorem~\ref{qlcl:thm:fixed-type} holds verbatim in the folded setting, with \(\Phi\) and \(\Gamma\) replaced by \(\Phi^W\) and \(\Gamma^W\), scalar witness matrices replaced by folded realizations \(M:B\to N\), and the same constants.
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Part (a) is Proposition~\ref{rsd:prop:folded-subcritical}.

For (b), let \(X=X^W_{\mathfrak V,U,T}\).  Since \(0<U\) is one of the quotient minors, the gap assumption gives \(\Phi^W(\mathfrak V,U,T)\ge\epsilon\), and Corollary~\ref{rsd:cor:folded-one-flag} gives \(\operatorname{\mathbb{E}} X\ge q^{\Phi^W(\mathfrak V,U,T)-2b^2}\).

For an ordered pair \((M,M')\) with \(row(J)=U\oplus U\), we have \(\ker J=U^\circ\oplus U^\circ\), so \(\dim J(B\oplus B)=2u\) and hence \(M(B)\cap M'(B)=0\): the two images are independent subspaces of \(\mathbb F_q^{ns}\).  The restrictions of the independent uniform rows of \(H_C\) and \(H_S\) to independent subspaces are independent, so the two indicator variables are independent and their covariance is zero.  For all remaining ordered pairs the covariance is at most the joint probability, and Lemma~\ref{rsd:lem:folded-dependent-pairs} bounds the sum of these joint probabilities.  Therefore
\[
   \operatorname{Var}(X)\le q^{2\Phi^W(\mathfrak V,U,T)-\epsilon+8b^2},
\]
and Chebyshev's inequality yields
\[
   \operatorname{Pr}[X=0]\le\frac{\operatorname{Var}(X)}{(\operatorname{\mathbb{E}} X)^2}\le q^{-\epsilon+12b^2}. \qedhere
\]
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- corollary-6: body_md -->
\label{rsd:cor:folded-uniform}
Define folded qLCL properties by finite families of folded profiles and sets of allowed logical row spaces in \(\mathcal L(B^*)\), exactly as in Definition~\ref{qlcl:def:qlcl-property}.  Then Theorem~\ref{qlcl:thm:qlcl-threshold} holds verbatim for \(\operatorname{\mathsf{PCSS}}^W(n,q;m_0,m_1)\), and Theorem~\ref{qlcl:thm:uniform-threshold} holds verbatim for \(\operatorname{\mathsf{Nest}}^W(n,q;m_0,m_1)\), with \(\Phi,\Gamma\) replaced by \(\Phi^W,\Gamma^W\), with the same constants, and with the same \(\gamma_q^{-1}\) conditioning loss.
<!-- end corollary-6 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
The union bounds over profiles and over the at most \(q^{2b^2}\) flags in \(B^*\) are unchanged, so the folded analogue of Theorem~\ref{qlcl:thm:qlcl-threshold} follows from Theorem~\ref{rsd:thm:folded-fixed-type} exactly as in the scalar case.  For the uniform ensemble, Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:conditioning} concerns only the parity checks on the scalar unfolding \(\mathbb F_q^{ns}\) and applies verbatim: conditioned on full rank, \(\operatorname{\mathsf{PCSS}}^W(n,q;m_0,m_1)\) is \(\operatorname{\mathsf{Nest}}^W(n,q;m_0,m_1)\), and the full-rank event has probability at least \(\gamma_q\).  Finally, the feasibility restriction in the analogue of~\eqref{qlcl:eq:Gmax-unif} is justified by the folded analogue of Lemma~\ref{qlcl:lem:auto-feasibility}, whose proof applies verbatim to a folded realization \(M:B\to N\) in a fixed nested pair \(S\subseteq N\): the image of \(K_S(M)=T^\circ\) under \(M\) is \(M(B)\cap S\), with kernel \(\ker M=U^\circ\), so \(\dim\bigl(M(B)\cap S\bigr)=u-t\le\dim S\), and the induced image of \(M(B)\) in \(N/S\) has dimension \(t\le\dim(N/S)\).
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
\label{rsd:rem:folded-consistency}
For \(s=1\) the fold is trivial: \(\operatorname{Hom}(B,\mathbb F_q)=B^*\), a folded profile is a scalar profile after the identification \(B\cong\mathbb F_q^b\), \(\operatorname{Hom}_U(B,\mathbb F_q)=U\), the folded mass~\eqref{eq:folded-mass} is the scalar mass~\eqref{qlcl:eq:profile-mass}, and Lemmas~\ref{rsd:lem:folded-exact-count}--\ref{rsd:lem:folded-dependent-pairs} together with Theorem~\ref{rsd:thm:folded-fixed-type} specialize to Lemmas~\ref{qlcl:lem:exact-row-count}, \ref{qlcl:lem:fixed-matrix-prob}, \ref{qlcl:lem:minor-potential}, \ref{qlcl:lem:pair-submodularity}, \ref{qlcl:lem:dependent-pairs}, and Theorem~\ref{qlcl:thm:fixed-type}.  The folded statements are therefore a strict generalization proved by the same argument, not a reduction to the scalar case.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- corollary-7: body_md -->
\label{cor:joint-form-folded}
For the event $E$ defined above, we have:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:prob-join-sat-folded}
    Pr_C[E(C, \mathcal F)] \le |\mathcal F|\cdot q^{4b^2} \cdot q^{-\delta sn}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-7 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
The corollary follows by union bounding over all $\mathfrak V \in \mathcal F$, $U_X,U_Z,T_X,T_Z$ satisfying the appropriate conditions, and then applying the folded version of Proposition~\ref{prop:fixed-type}.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{rsd:lem:kernel-mass}
For every \(U\le V\),
\[
      \dim\bigl(\mathcal Z_i(V_i)\cap\operatorname{Hom}_U(V^*,W)\bigr)
      =s\dim(U\cap V_i),
\]
and hence
\[
      a_{\mathcal Z(V)}(U)=s\sum_{i=1}^n\dim(U\cap V_i).
\]
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
A map \(f:V^*\to W\) lies in \(\mathcal Z_i(V_i)\cap\operatorname{Hom}_U(V^*,W)\) precisely when it vanishes on both \(V_i^\circ\) and \(U^\circ\), hence on \(V_i^\circ+U^\circ\).  Since
\[
      (V_i^\circ+U^\circ)^\circ=V_i\cap U,
\]
the quotient \(V^*/(V_i^\circ+U^\circ)\) has dimension \(\dim(V_i\cap U)\).  The space of maps from this quotient to \(W\) has dimension \(s\dim(V_i\cap U)\).
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
\label{rsd:rem:classical-special-cases}
The framework specializes cleanly to both classical theories.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=2em,label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item \emph{Classical scalar LCL.}  Set $S=0$ and take an ordinary linear code $C\le\mathbb F_q^n$ of dimension $m$.  Then $K_S(A)=\ker(A)$ for every witness matrix $A$, so the logical row space is automatically the ordinary row space: $T=U$.  For scalar local profiles one obtains
\[
   \Phi_{0,m}(\mathcal V,U,U)=a_\mathcal V(U)-(n-m)\dim U,
\]
and for every proper $W<U$,
\[
   \Phi_{0,m}(\mathcal V,U,U)-\Phi_{0,m}(\mathcal V,W,W)
   =a_\mathcal V(U)-a_\mathcal V(W)-(n-m)(\dim U-\dim W).
\]
This is the LCL potential increment for random linear codes in the sense of Levi--Mosheiff--Shagrithaya~\cite[Section~4]{LMS25}.  Thus the quotient threshold theorem reduces, after the harmless relabeling $T=U$, to the classical fixed-width LCL threshold.

\item \emph{Ordinary folded subspace designs.}  Again set $S=0$, but allow a folded alphabet $W$ and restrict local constraints to kernel profiles $\mathcal Z_i(V_i)$.  The injective-logical condition is automatic for every nonzero represented subspace, because no nonzero vector is a stabilizer.  If $\dim N=\alpha ns$, then
\[
   \frac{1}{sn}\Phi^W_{0,\alpha ns}(\mathcal Z(V),U,U)
   =\frac1n\sum_i\dim(U\cap V_i)-(1-\alpha)\dim U
   =\Phi_V(U,(V_i),\alpha).
\]
The relative CSS definition below is obtained by keeping the same folded kernel-profile tests but allowing $S\ne0$ and explicitly requiring the tested representative subspace to intersect $S$ trivially.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- definition-25: body_md -->
\label{rsd:def:relative}
Let \(S\subseteq N\subseteq W^n\), let \(r\in\mathbb N\), and let \(\alpha\in[0,1]\).  The pair \((N,S)\) is an \emph{\(\alpha\)-relative subspace design up to dimension \(r\)} if for every subspace \(A\le N\) satisfying
\[
  1\le \dim A\le r,
  \qquad A\cap S=\{0\},
\]
one has
\begin{equation}\label{rsd:eq:relative-design}
   \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \dim(A\cap K_i)
      \le \alpha\dim A .
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\[
   \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n \dim\pi_i(A)
      \ge (1-\alpha)\dim A .
\]
<!-- end definition-25 -->
<!-- definition-26: body_md -->
\label{rsd:def:css-sd}
Let \(Q=Q(C_1,C_2)\) be the CSS code defined by \(C_2\subseteq C_1\subseteq W^n\).  We say that \(Q\) is an \emph{\((\alpha_X,\alpha_Z)\)-CSS subspace design up to dimension \(r\)} if
\[
   (C_1,C_2)\quad\text{is an }\alpha_X\text{-relative subspace design up to dimension }r,
\]
and
\[
   (C_2^\perp,C_1^\perp)\quad\text{is an }\alpha_Z\text{-relative subspace design up to dimension }r.
\]
<!-- end definition-26 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
\label{rsd:rem:not-quotient-design}
The quotient $N/S$ is the logical space, but its coordinates are not obtained by quotienting each folded coordinate independently.  A logical coset can have many physical representatives with different zero patterns.  Therefore the design condition must test an actual representative subspace $A\le N$ and only then require $A\cap S=0$.  This is the same order of operations used throughout quotient LCL: local constraints are imposed before quotienting, while independence is measured after quotienting.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{rsd:prop:section}
Let \(q_N:N\to N/S\) be the quotient map.  The pair \((N,S)\) is an \(\alpha\)-relative subspace design up to dimension \(r\) if and only if for every \(B\le N/S\) with \(1\le \dim B\le r\) and every linear section \(\sigma:B\to N\) of \(q_N\),
\[
   \frac1n\sum_i \dim(\sigma(B)\cap K_i)
      \le \alpha\dim B .
\]
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
If \(A\le N\) and \(A\cap S=0\), then \(q_N|_A:A\to q_N(A)\) is an isomorphism, so \(A\) is the image of the section \((q_N|_A)^{-1}\).  Conversely, the image of any section intersects \(S\) trivially.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{rsd:prop:inherit}
If \(N\le W^n\) is an ordinary \(\alpha\)-subspace-design code up to dimension \(r\), then \((N,S)\) is an \(\alpha\)-relative subspace design up to dimension \(r\) for every \(S\subseteq N\).
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
The ordinary condition is imposed on every low-dimensional \(A\le N\).  The relative condition is imposed only on those \(A\) satisfying \(A\cap S=0\).
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{rsd:prop:monotone}
Let \(S\subseteq N\).  If \((N,S)\) is an \(\alpha\)-relative design up to dimension \(r\), then \((N',S\cap N')\) is an \(\alpha\)-relative design up to dimension \(r\) for every \(N'\subseteq N\).  Also, if \(S\subseteq S'\subseteq N\), then \((N,S')\) is an \(\alpha\)-relative design up to dimension \(r\).
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
Both statements reduce the collection of subspaces \(A\) that must be tested.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{rsd:prop:distance}
If \((N,S)\) is an \(\alpha\)-relative subspace design up to dimension \(1\), then every \(x\in N\setminus S\) satisfies
\[
   \frac{\operatorname{wt}(x)}n\ge 1-\alpha .
\]
Consequently, if \(Q(C_1,C_2)\) is an \((\alpha_X,\alpha_Z)\)-CSS subspace design up to dimension \(1\), then
\[
   \frac{d_X}{n}\ge 1-\alpha_X,
   \qquad
   \frac{d_Z}{n}\ge 1-\alpha_Z.
\]
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Let \(x\in N\setminus S\) and set \(A=\operatorname{span}\{x\}\).  Then \(A\cap S=0\).  Moreover \(\dim(A\cap K_i)=1\) exactly when \(x_i=0\), and is zero otherwise.  Thus
\[
  1-\frac{\operatorname{wt}(x)}n
   =\frac1n\sum_i\dim(A\cap K_i)
   \le \alpha.
\]
Apply this to \((C_1,C_2)\) and \((C_2^\perp,C_1^\perp)\).
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
For a balanced CSS code of quantum rate \(R\), the two normalizer rates are naturally around \((1+R)/2\).  Thus a near-optimal CSS subspace design has \(\alpha_X,\alpha_Z\approx(1+R)/2\), and Proposition~\ref{rsd:prop:distance} yields relative distance close to \((1-R)/2\), the quantum Singleton scale.  Folded CSS codes with Singleton-scale relative distance are already known via quantum AEL distance amplification~\cite{BGG24,BJMST24}; the design condition strengthens the distance bound from dimension one to all dimensions up to \(r\).
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- definition-27: body_md -->
\label{rsd:def:profile}
Let \(S\subseteq N\subseteq W^n\).  A tuple \((V_1,\ldots,V_n)\in\mathcal L(V)^n\) is a \emph{relative \(V\)-profile contained in \((N,S)\)} if there are a subspace \(A\le N\) and an isomorphism \(\phi:V\to A^*\) such that
\[
      A\cap S=0
\]
and, for every coordinate \(i\),
\begin{equation}\label{rsd:eq:profile-containment}
      \phi(V_i)^\circ\subseteq A\cap K_i .
\end{equation}
<!-- end definition-27 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{rsd:prop:lcl-contained-profile}
Let \(S\subseteq N\subseteq W^n\), let \(V\) be finite-dimensional, and put \(B=V^*\).  A tuple \((V_i)_{i=1}^n\in\mathcal L(V)^n\) is a relative \(V\)-profile contained in \((N,S)\) if and only if \((S,N)\) has a folded qLCL realization \(M:B\to N\) with local constraints \(\mathcal Z_i(V_i)\), ordinary row space \(R(M)=V\), and logical row space \(\Lambda_S(M)=V\), after identifying \(B^*=V\).
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
Suppose first that the profile is contained, witnessed by \(A\le N\) and \(\phi:V\to A^*\).  Dualizing \(\phi\) gives an isomorphism \(\phi^*:A\to V^*=B\), hence its inverse gives a map \(M:B\to A\subseteq N\).  Because \(M\) is injective, \(R(M)=V\).  Because \(A\cap S=0\), we have \(K_S(M)=\ker M=0\), hence \(\Lambda_S(M)=V\).  For coordinate \(i\), the condition \(\phi(V_i)^\circ\subseteq A\cap K_i\) is equivalent, after transporting through \(M\), to \(V_i^\circ\subseteq\ker(\pi_iM)\).  Therefore \(M_i\in\mathcal Z_i(V_i)\).

Conversely, let \(M:B\to N\) be such a folded qLCL realization and set \(A=M(B)\).  Since \(R(M)=B^*=V\), the map \(M\) is injective.  Since \(\Lambda_S(M)=R(M)\), we have \(M^{-1}(S)=\ker M=0\), so \(A\cap S=0\).  The inverse map \(M^{-1}:A\to B=V^*\) dualizes to an isomorphism \(\phi:V\to A^*\).  The local constraint \(V_i^\circ\subseteq\ker(\pi_iM)\) says exactly that \(\phi(V_i)^\circ\subseteq A\cap K_i\).  Hence the profile is contained.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
\label{rsd:thm:profile-characterization}
Let \(S\subseteq N\subseteq W^n\).  The pair \((N,S)\) is an \(\alpha\)-relative subspace design up to dimension \(r\) if and only if for every vector space \(V\) with \(\dim V\le r\) and every relative \(V\)-profile \((V_1,\ldots,V_n)\) contained in \((N,S)\),
\[
      \Phi_V(V,(V_i),\alpha)\ge0.
\]
Equivalently, \((N,S)\) has no injective-logical kernel-profile witness whose associated design profile has negative normalized design potential \(\Phi_V(V,(V_i),\alpha)\).  When \(\alpha=\dim N/(ns)\), this is exactly absence of negative normalized folded qLCL potential; for general \(\alpha\) the two potentials are related by~\eqref{eq:potential-slack}.
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
Assume first that \((N,S)\) is a relative design, and let the profile be witnessed by \(A\le N\) and \(\phi:V\to A^*\).  From \(\phi(V_i)^\circ\subseteq A\cap K_i\),
\[
   \dim(A\cap K_i)
      \ge \dim\phi(V_i)^\circ
      =\dim V-\dim V_i.
\]
Since \(A\cap S=0\) and \(\dim A=\dim V\le r\),
\[
  \frac1n\sum_i(\dim V-\dim V_i)
      \le \frac1n\sum_i\dim(A\cap K_i)
      \le \alpha\dim V.
\]
This is exactly \(\Phi_V(V,(V_i),\alpha)\ge0\).

Conversely, suppose the relative-design condition fails.  Then there is \(A\le N\), \(A\cap S=0\), \(1\le t=\dim A\le r\), such that
\[
   \frac1n\sum_i\dim(A\cap K_i)>\alpha t.
\]
Set \(V=A^*\), let \(\phi\) be the identity map \(V\to A^*\), and define
\[
   V_i\coloneqq(A\cap K_i)^\circ\le A^*=V.
\]
Then \(\phi(V_i)^\circ=A\cap K_i\), so the profile is contained, and
\[
   \Phi_V(V,(V_i),\alpha)
     =\alpha t-\frac1n\sum_i\dim(A\cap K_i)<0.
\]
The final equivalence follows from Proposition~\ref{rsd:prop:lcl-contained-profile} and the definition of the design potential.  If \(\alpha=\dim N/(ns)\), this is the exact normalized qLCL potential by~\eqref{eq:potential-dictionary}; otherwise the comparison is the slack identity~\eqref{eq:potential-slack}.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{rsd:lem:minimal-bad}
If \((N,S)\) is not an \(\alpha\)-relative subspace design up to dimension \(r\), then there exist a vector space \(V\) with \(1\le\dim V\le r\) and a contained relative \(V\)-profile \((V_i)\) such that
\[
      \Phi_V(U,(V_i),\alpha)<0
      \qquad\text{for every nonzero }U\le V.
\]
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{rsd:thm:profile-characterization}, there is a contained profile \((V_i)\) with \(\Phi_V(V,(V_i),\alpha)<0\).  Among all subspaces \(W\le V\) maximizing \(\Phi_V(W,(V_i),\alpha)\), choose one of maximum dimension.  Since \(\Phi_V(0,(V_i),\alpha)=0\) and \(\Phi_V(V,(V_i),\alpha)<0\), this maximizer is a proper subspace of \(V\).

Let \(\bar V=V/W\) and \(\bar V_i=(V_i+W)/W\).  We claim that \((\bar V_i)\) is contained.  Suppose \((V_i)\) is witnessed by \(A\le N\) and \(\phi:V\to A^*\).  Let
\[
      A'\coloneqq \phi(W)^\circ\le A.
\]
Then \(A'\cap S=0\), and restriction of functionals gives a natural isomorphism \(\bar\phi:\bar V\to(A')^*\).  Moreover
\[
      \bar\phi(\bar V_i)^\circ
      =A'\cap\phi(V_i)^\circ
      \subseteq A'\cap K_i,
\]
so the quotient profile is contained in \((N,S)\).

For any nonzero \(\bar U\le\bar V\), write \(\bar U=(U+W)/W\) with \(U\not\subseteq W\).  A direct dimension calculation gives
\[
      \Phi_{\bar V}(\bar U,(\bar V_i),\alpha)
      =\Phi_V(U+W,(V_i),\alpha)-\Phi_V(W,(V_i),\alpha).
\]
The maximality of \(W\), together with the choice of maximum dimension among maximizers, implies that the right-hand side is negative whenever \(U+W\supsetneq W\).  Hence every nonzero subspace of the quotient has negative potential.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- definition-28: body_md -->
\label{rsd:def:bounded-profile-class}
Fix \(r\).  A folded profile class
\(\mathscr F_{\le r}=\{\mathscr F_t\}_{1\le t\le r}\) assigns, for each
\(t\), a collection \(\mathscr F_t\) of length-\(d\) folded profiles on a fixed
\(t\)-dimensional coefficient space.  We say that it has entropy exponent
\(h\) if
\[
       |\mathscr F_t|\le q^{h d}
       \qquad\text{for every }1\le t\le r .
\]
Profiles on another \(t\)-dimensional coefficient space are identified with
members of \(\mathscr F_t\) after choosing a linear isomorphism.  This convention
only changes the estimates by the usual \(q^{O(r^2)}\) number of bases, which is
absorbed in the entropy term below.
<!-- end definition-28 -->
<!-- definition-29: body_md -->
\label{rsd:def:ael-robust}
Let \(\mathscr F_{\le r}\) be a folded profile class.  The pair
\((N,S)\) is \emph{AEL-robust \((\alpha,\mathscr F_{\le r})\) folded
LCL up to dimension \(r\)} if the following holds.  For every coefficient
space \(B\) with \(1\le\dim B\le r\), every profile
\(\mathfrak V\in\mathscr F_{\dim B}\), and every linear map
\(T:B\to N\) such that
\[
       \pi_\ell T\in \mathfrak V_\ell
       \qquad(\ell=1,\ldots,d),
\]
either
\[
       q_N(T(B))=0,
\]
or there is a nonzero subspace \(U\le B^*\) such that
\[
       \widehat\Phi^W_\alpha(U,\mathfrak V)\ge0 .
\]
Equivalently, if all nonzero subprofiles have negative potential, then every
realization of that profile inside \(N\) is logically trivial modulo \(S\).
<!-- end definition-29 -->
<!-- definition-30: body_md -->
\label{rsd:def:robust}
The pair \((N,S)\) is an \emph{AEL-robust \(\alpha\)-relative subspace design
up to dimension \(r\)} if the following holds.  For every vector space \(V\)
with \(1\le t=\dim V\le r\), every vector space \(A\) with \(\dim A=t\), every
isomorphism \(\phi:V\to A^*\), every linear map \(T:A\to N\), and every tuple
\((V_1,\ldots,V_d)\in\mathcal L(V)^d\) satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{rsd:eq:robust-containment}
   \phi(V_\ell)^\circ\subseteq \ker(\pi_\ell\circ T)
   \qquad(\ell=1,\ldots,d),
\end{equation}
either
\[
   q_N(T(A))=0,
\]
or there is a nonzero \(U\le V\) such that
\[
   \Phi_V(U,(V_\ell)_{\ell=1}^d,\alpha)\ge0.
\]
Here \(\Phi_V\) is the subspace-profile potential~\eqref{eq:subspace-profile-potential}, with the tuple length \(d\) in place of \(n\) in the normalization.
<!-- end definition-30 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{rsd:prop:kernel-specialization}
Let \(\mathscr K_{\le r}\) be the profile class consisting, for each
\(t\le r\), of all kernel profiles
\[
      \bigl(\mathcal Z_1(V_1),\ldots,\mathcal Z_d(V_d)\bigr),
      \qquad V_\ell\le V,
      \qquad \dim V=t,
\]
with \(B=V^*\).  Then \(\mathscr K_{\le r}\) has entropy exponent at most
\(r^2\).  Moreover, for kernel profiles the potential
\eqref{rsd:eq:lcl-potential} agrees with the subspace-profile potential:
\[
      \widehat\Phi^W_\alpha(U,\mathcal Z_1(V_1),\ldots,\mathcal Z_d(V_d))
       = \Phi_V(U,(V_\ell)_{\ell=1}^d,\alpha).
\]
Consequently AEL-robust \((\alpha,\mathscr K_{\le r})\) folded LCL is
exactly AEL-robust \(\alpha\)-relative subspace design in the sense of
Definition~\ref{rsd:def:robust}.
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
The number of subspaces of a \(t\)-dimensional vector space is at most
\(q^{t^2}\), so the number of length-\(d\) kernel profiles is at most
\(q^{dt^2}\le q^{dr^2}\).  The potential identity is Lemma~\ref{rsd:lem:kernel-mass},
divided by \(sd\).  Transporting the coefficient space through the isomorphism
\(\phi:V\to A^*\) identifies the containment condition
\eqref{rsd:eq:robust-containment} with the requirement
\(\pi_\ell T\in\mathcal Z_\ell(V_\ell)\).  Under the same identification the nonnegative
subprofile condition is exactly the displayed potential condition.  This proves
the equivalence of the folded-LCL and kernel-profile formulations.
